repo.description: ### Summary An OS command injection vulnerability exists in the `commitlint.yml` workflow. By crafting a malicious Pull Request title, an attacker can break out of a bash `echo` statement and execute arbitrary commands on the GitHub Actions runner. Because this workflow uses the `pull_request` trigger, the execution is safely confined to a sandboxed environment with a read-only token, but it still represents an unintended Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE) flaw. ### Details In the `Commitlint` workflow, the Pull Request title is directly interpolated into a bash script using the `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` context expression: ```yaml - name: Commitlint on PR title run: echo '${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}' | npx commitlint ``` GitHub Actions evaluates and substitutes `${{ ... }}` expressions before the bash shell executes the command. If a PR title contains a single quote (`'`), it prematurely closes the bash string definition. An attacker can then append a semicolon (`;`) followed by arbitrary bash commands, which the runner will blindly execute. ### PoC 1. Fork the repository and open a new Pull Request (or edit the title of an existing one). 2. Set the title of the Pull Request to the following exact payload: ```text test'; echo "=== PWNED ==="; echo "Execution User: $(whoami)"; echo ' ``` 3. The `Commitlint` workflow will trigger automatically. 4. Go to the Actions tab and check the workflow execution logs under the **Commitlint on PR title** step. You will see the injected commands successfully executed before the pipeline fails or finishes: ### Impact - **Vulnerability Type:** OS Command Injection / Arbitrary Code Execution (CWE-78). - **Impact Level:** Low/Medium. An external attacker can execute arbitrary code on the GitHub Actions runner. However, because the workflow is triggered via `pull_request` (and not `pull_request_target`), the runner operates in an isolated, sandboxed environment without access to repository secrets, and the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` is strictly read-only. Therefore, there is no direct risk of source code modification or secret exfiltration. - **Mitigation:** Never interpolate untrusted GitHub context variables directly into inline bash scripts. Instead, bind them safely via environment variables: ```yaml - name: Commitlint on PR title env: PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} run: echo "$PR_TITLE" | npx commitlint ```
repo.summary: OS command injection vulnerability exists in the Commitlint workflow
